kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-01.title: Tick off the digits
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-01.body:
Go through the digits 0 to 9 and look for each one in the picture (some are turned around). You can find 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8. The digits 6 and 9 are not there.

**Answer: (D) 6 and 9**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-01.title: Check the options
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-01.body:
3, 5, 4, 8, 2, 0, 7 and 1 can all be found in the picture, so options A, B, C and E name digits that are there. Only 6 and 9 are missing.

**Answer: (D) 6 and 9**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-02.title: Take away
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-02.body:
Four children take one book each, so 4 books are taken: $12 - 4 = 8$ books are left.

**Answer: (B) 8**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-03.title: Exactly six
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-03.body:
Less than seven but more than five means exactly 6 dots. Count the dots on each dress: only dress A has 6.

**Answer: (A)**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-04.title: Legs per animal
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-04.body:
Lions have 4 legs: $2 \times 4 = 8$. Dolphins have no legs: 0. Eagles have 2 legs: $4 \times 2 = 8$. Altogether $8 + 0 + 8 = 16$.

**Answer: (C) 16**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-05.title: Groups of five
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-05.body:
20 tulips are $20 \div 5 = 4$ groups of 5. Each group takes 10 minutes: $4 \times 10 = 40$ minutes. Starting at 9:00 they finish at 9:40.

**Answer: (C) At 9:40**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-08.title: Row by row
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-08.body:
The inside is a plus shape. Count its squares row by row from the top: 1, 1, 5, 1, 1. Altogether $1 + 1 + 5 + 1 + 1 = 9$ tiles.

**Answer: (E) 9**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-09.title: Close the gap
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-09.body:
Cat is on the first tile and Mouse is 6 tiles ahead of it. With every jump Cat gets 2 tiles further and Mouse 1, so the gap shrinks by 1. After 6 jumps Cat catches Mouse.

In 6 jumps Mouse moves 6 tiles. Counting 6 tiles on from Mouse brings it to the tile marked 4. (Check: Cat moves 12 tiles from the start and lands there too.)

**Answer: (D) 4**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-10.title: Test the options
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-10.body:
All options are tens, and none is 10. Add 30: $20 + 30 = 50$ is less than 60, but $30 + 30 = 60$ is not. So the number is 20.

**Answer: (A) 20**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-11.title: Corners and streets
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-11.body:
There are 4 corner houses. There are 4 streets, and each gets 2 new houses: $4 \times 2 = 8$. Altogether $4 + 8 = 12$ houses.

**Answer: (B) 12**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-12.title: List the family
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-12.body:
The children are Kasia, her 3 sisters and her 3 brothers (one of them is Mike). Mike's brothers are the other 2 boys. Mike's sisters are Kasia and her 3 sisters: 4 girls.

**Answer: (E) 2 brothers and 4 sisters**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-13.title: Look at each face
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-13.body:
Each face of the large cube is a 3 × 3 square. When a corner cube is taken away, the 3 faces that meet at that corner each lose a corner square. So every stamp is a 3 × 3 square with some corners missing.

In the picture the removed cubes are the top front left, the bottom front right and the two top back corners. Go through the 6 faces:

- Front: top left and bottom right missing (two opposite corners).
- Back and left: two corners on the same side missing.
- Top: three corners missing.
- Bottom: one corner missing.
- Right: two opposite corners missing.

So stamps with 1 missing corner, 2 missing corners on one side, 2 opposite missing corners and 3 missing corners can be made. No face has all 4 corners missing, so the plus-shaped stamp is impossible. That is 4 stamps.

**Answer: (D) 4**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-14.title: Fill it completely
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-14.body:
The square has 16 cells and each piece covers 4, so at most 4 pieces fit. Four pieces do fit:

- One T along the top: the top row's left 3 cells and the cell below the middle one.
- One T in the same way along the bottom, turned upside down, using the bottom row's right 3 cells.
- Two more T's, standing upright, fill the left and right sides.

All 16 cells are covered, so 0 cells are left empty.

**Answer: (A) 0**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-15.title: Change into plums
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-15.body:
1 pear = 2 apples = $2 \times 3 = 6$ plums. 6 plums are $6 \div 2 = 3$ strawberries. So 1 pear = 3 strawberries, and 6 pears = $6 \times 3 = 18$ strawberries.

**Answer: (C) 18**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-16.title: First house and the rest
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-16.body:
The first house uses 6 matchsticks: 2 for the roof, 1 under the roof, 2 walls and 1 floor. Every next house shares a wall with the house before, so it needs only 5 more: 2 roof, 1 under the roof, 1 wall and 1 floor.

10 houses: $6 + 9 \times 5 = 6 + 45 = 51$.

**Answer: (B) 51**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-17.title: Find the size
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-17.body:
Around the edge of a square of 6 × 6 pieces there are $6 + 6 + 4 + 4 = 20$ pieces, so the box is 6 by 6 and each layer has 36 pieces.

The upper layer still has $36 - 20 = 16$ pieces in the middle, and the lower layer has all 36. Left: $16 + 36 = 52$.

**Answer: (D) 52**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-18.title: Try the options
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-18.body:
There are 4 vehicles. With 2 bikes there are 2 strollers: $2 \times 2 + 2 \times 4 = 4 + 8 = 12$ wheels. ✓

**Answer: (B) 2**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-18.title: Start with bikes
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0102-18.body:
If all 4 were bikes there would be 8 wheels. There are $12 - 8 = 4$ extra wheels, and each stroller has 2 more wheels than a bike, so there are 2 strollers and $4 - 2 = 2$ bikes.

**Answer: (B) 2**
